---
title: "Week 12: Databases and web hosting"
---

Use the Census data you already have to learn spatial SQL, then turn the analysis into a public-facing report and website.

## 1. Create and query a spatial database

[Open the DuckDB Spatial tutorial](lecture-12A.html)

Connect Python to a persistent database, import the Week 11 Census points and district polygons, ask location and distance questions, join by geometry, and export maps and summaries.

<a href="lecture-12A.ipynb" download>Download the database notebook</a>

## 2. Turn the analysis into a website

[Open the publishing tutorial](lecture-12B.html)

Render a notebook with Quarto, use ChatGPT prompts or a reusable skill to help create a website, preview through localhost, then publish the generated files with GitHub Pages.

<a href="lecture-12B.ipynb" download>Download the publishing notes</a>

## 3. Build a full-stack GIS with Python

[Open the full-stack GIS demo](lecture-12C.html)

Connect a Leaflet web map to FastAPI and DuckDB Spatial. Filter historical district counts and click a location to query Census sample dots within a radius.

<a href="lecture-12C.ipynb" download>Download lecture 12C</a> · [Download the complete runnable project](downloads/census-full-stack.zip)

## Start here

- **Download both datasets into `week12/data`:** [census_sample.parquet](../week11-large-data-viz-lidar/data/samples/census_sample.parquet) and [districts_2015.geojson](../week11-large-data-viz-lidar/data/samples/districts_2015.geojson). Create the local folders first and move the files there if your browser saves them to Downloads.
- Save the notebooks in `week12`; extract the full-stack project into `week12/census-full-stack`.
- **Keep using `geospatial`:** follow Part A to install DuckDB/PyArrow, and Part C to add FastAPI/Uvicorn/HTTPX in the same environment.
- [Dependency reference](environment.yml).
- [Download this tutorial folder](downloads/week12-tutorials.zip).
- [Standalone website starter](downloads/starter-website.zip).
- [Quarto website starter](downloads/quarto-site.zip).
- [Reusable skill example](downloads/census-story-site-skill.zip).
- [Setup and folder instructions](README.md).

The Census dots are synthetic historical teaching data; their counts are not population estimates or current demographics. All three tutorials keep that distinction visible.
